subject: Uptime bands and latency guardrails for Helios - proposed template
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Helios SLA template - quick prep before outreach

Ben —

Sophie is asking us to move the baseline uptime from 99.9% to 99.95% and wants credits to kick in at a smaller delta than our standard template. Before you send a formal update, can legal and infra weigh in on two things: 1) whether we can accept a 99.95% baseline for a negotiated enterprise term, and 2) whether we can keep monthly credit caps as-is (2x monthly fee) but change the banding so credits start at 99.95 rather than 99.9.

Operationally, Aditya — will that materially increase our risk/exposure for noisy transient issues? If so, what mitigations would you recommend (maintenance windows, regional carveouts, auto-failover language)?

Attached is the draft we used for recent mid-market deals (redwood-proposed-uptime-bands-20250503.pdf). I also pulled Helios' redlines from the call and attached them (helios-redlines-20250503.docx).

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

-----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: Helios Analytics Procurement <procurement@helios-analytics.com>
Date: 2025-05-03T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood - Proposed uptime bands & latency guardrails (for Helios)

Hi Sophie — great to connect earlier. Per our call I promised a concise proposal on availability bands and the monthly credit schedule so your procurement team can surface the ask internally. High level: Redwood can accommodate a slightly tighter baseline for an annual commitment if we agree on linear credit banding and a hard cap on monthly credits. Below is the suggested text we can incorporate into the Master Services Agreement (MSA).

Proposed availability & credit schedule (recommended):
- Baseline availability: 99.95% monthly (measured across routed production traffic).
- Credit trigger: If monthly availability is below 99.95%, customer is eligible for credits per the band below.
- Bands & credits (percent of monthly invoice):
  - 99.95% - 99.90% -> 10% credit
  - 99.90% - 99.50% -> 25% credit
  - <99.50% -> 50% credit
- Monthly credit cap: Credits will not exceed 2x the affected monthly service fees.

Latency guardrails (service-level objectives):
- P95 response time for text generation API under normal load: <= 120 ms.
- Latency credits will only be issued if availability credit criteria is not met AND sustained P95 > 250 ms for a rolling 24-hour window. Latency alone will not trigger full availability credits; this is to avoid double-recovery.

Operational carveouts & mitigations:
- We request a mutually agreed maintenance window (2x/month, up to 4 hours each) that is excluded from availability calculations if customer is notified 72 hours in advance.
- Regional outage fallback: Redwood will provide temporary regional failover when possible; if failover increases latency beyond the thresholds, it will be treated as a separate incident with root-cause reporting but will not automatically increase credit above the banded schedule.

Next steps: If this looks directionally acceptable, I can share a tracked-changes MSA and a one-page schedule for signatures. If procurement wants the baseline at 99.98% or to remove the monthly cap, we will need executive sign-off.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-uptime-bands-20250503.pdf

-----
From: Sophie Park <sophie@helios-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Analytics Procurement <procurement@helios-analytics.com>
Date: 2025-05-03T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood - Proposed uptime bands & latency guardrails (for Helios)

Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear bands. A few notes from my side after running this past our SRE and procurement teams: 

1) Baseline: 99.95% is acceptable as a negotiating starting point. We would prefer the first credit band to start at 99.97% (i.e., 99.98-99.97 -> small credit) because our workload is customer-facing for SLAs we promise to our clients.
2) Cap: We understand caps are needed, but 2x monthly feels low for us given the downstream SLA obligations we carry. Is there room to increase the cap to 3x for the first 12 months of the contract (trial/transition period) and revert to 2x thereafter?
3) Latency: We appreciate the guardrail logic. Can we make latency credits more granular (P95 and P99 buckets) rather than tying them to availability credits only? Even so, we accept the combined approach if there is a defined exceptions process for incidents where latency materially impacts customer-facing queries.

We'll attach our redlines (see attached helios-redlines-20250503.docx). If Redwood can accept the 3x cap for the first year and add a narrow 99.97% band at the top, procurement can move faster.

Best,
Sophie Park
SRE Lead
Helios Analytics

-----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-03T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood - Proposed uptime bands & latency guardrails (for Helios) — counter from Helios

Looping you all in — Sophie pushed back with three asks: 1) add a 99.97% top band, 2) 3x monthly cap for year one, 3) more granular latency crediting.

My suggested path: we can accept the 99.97% mini-band (small credit 5%) as a commercial concession without infra risk; that helps procurement. For the 3x cap, I think we could agree to it for a 12-month transition if Legal adds a clear carveout that the increased cap is limited to availability credits caused by platform incidents (not customer misconfigurations). Aditya — can you confirm whether a 3x cap materially increases exposure in terms of balancing reserves / SRE response obligations?

Laura — if this is acceptable from a legal exposure perspective with the carveout language, I'll propose the tracked MSA and a 12-month trial clause. Quick turnaround requested — Sophie indicated procurement wants to move next week.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Quoted attachments: helios-redlines-20250503.docx
